sourceLaws.title: User Path Ledger Foundation
sourceLaws.failureMode: No single authoritative memory for user approval and denial decisions at the action boundary.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Require one authoritative User Path Ledger as the only decision-memory source for user-originated action-law outcomes.
sourceLaws.stateForm: UPL exists as one authoritative store for user path decisions.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one authoritative User Path Ledger for approved and denied paths.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: foundation of one authoritative User Path Ledger.

sourceLaws.title: Approved and Denied Partition
sourceLaws.failureMode: Approved and denied user path decisions blend into one store and become ambiguous during enforcement.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Partition the User Path Ledger into approved paths and denied paths so downstream lookup remains unambiguous.
sourceLaws.stateForm: UPL = approved_paths union denied_paths with no ambiguous overlap.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires approved and denied path partitions inside the User Path Ledger.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: approved and denied sections are partitioned.

sourceLaws.title: Approval Becomes Active Law
sourceLaws.failureMode: User approval happens but is not persisted as active law, causing repeat prompts and continuity loss.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: When the user says yes, write the approved path into the approved section with ACTIVE status as the law-creation event itself.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires user approvals to become active approved-path law entries automatically.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: approval automatically becomes active law.

sourceLaws.title: Denial Fork Prompt
sourceLaws.failureMode: A denial is treated as permanent or forgotten without asking whether it should become standing law.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: When the user says no, ask exactly once whether that denial should become a permanent law.
sourceLaws.stateForm: Deny(path) => fork to permanent-denial question exactly once.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one explicit denial-law fork after a user denial.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: denial forks once into permanent-law decision.

sourceLaws.title: Permanent Denial Law
sourceLaws.failureMode: Permanent denials are not granted equal enforcement force to approvals.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: If the user says yes to permanent denial, write the denied path into the denied section as enforceable law.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires permanent denials to become active denied-path law entries.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: permanent denials become enforceable law.

sourceLaws.title: One-Time Denial Event
sourceLaws.failureMode: One-time denials accidentally persist into future blocking behavior.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: If the user rejects permanent denial, record the denial as a one-time event with no future enforcement.
sourceLaws.stateForm: TemporaryDeny(path) => log event without future deny-law activation.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires one-time denials to remain logged but non-binding going forward.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: one-time denials are logged without future enforcement.

sourceLaws.title: Pre-Prompt Ledger Lookup
sourceLaws.failureMode: The system prompts the user repeatedly even when prior path decisions already exist.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Require the NSL to check the User Path Ledger before prompting the user for approval.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires prior decision lookup before any new approval prompt is shown.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: NSL checks the ledger before prompting.

sourceLaws.title: Visible Entries Only
sourceLaws.failureMode: Hidden ledger entries shape enforcement without user visibility.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Require every User Path Ledger entry to remain visible to the user.
sourceLaws.stateForm: forall entry in UPL: visible_to_user(entry) = true.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity forbids hidden User Path Ledger entries.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: all entries are user-visible.

sourceLaws.title: Witnessed Modification
sourceLaws.failureMode: Ledger entries change silently without a witnessed modification history.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Allow the user to modify entries only through witnessed modification events.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires user-driven entry modification to be witnessed, not silently overwritten.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL specification: modifications are witnessed events.

sourceLaws.title: Mute Without Deletion
sourceLaws.failureMode: Muted paths require destructive deletion instead of reversible suspension.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Allow the user to set an entry to MUTED so lookups skip it without deleting historical record.
sourceLaws.stateForm: Mute(entry) => entry.status = MUTED and lookup skips entry.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires muted entries to be non-enforcing but still preserved.

sourceLaws.title: Canonical Path Identity

sourceLaws.title: Deterministic Conflict Precedence
sourceLaws.failureMode: Conflicting approved and denied entries resolve nondeterministically across scope and specificity.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Resolve User Path Ledger conflicts by deterministic precedence: exact canonical path outranks DOMAIN, DOMAIN outranks GLOBAL, active denial outranks active approval at the same specificity, and only witnessed user overrides can replace an existing decision at equal specificity.
sourceLaws.stateForm: Precedence = ExactPath > DOMAIN > GLOBAL; same_scope_conflict => DENY > APPROVE unless witnessed user override replaces same-scope entry.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires deterministic precedence across approved and denied entries so enforcement cannot drift by implementation.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL hardening: deterministic conflict precedence across path scope and polarity.

sourceLaws.title: Decision Boundary Binding
sourceLaws.failureMode: A remembered approval or denial replays outside the original user-intended arguments, targets, recipients, or resource limits.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Bind every remembered decision to its canonical action fingerprint, argument boundary, recipient set, target class, effect class, and resource ceiling so anything outside that bound requires a fresh user decision.
sourceLaws.stateForm: UPL.entry(path) => {canonical_fingerprint, arg_boundary, recipient_set, target_class, effect_class, resource_ceiling}.
sourceLaws.outputForm: Agent Buccet time continuity requires approval and denial memory to stay bound to the original decision boundary rather than widening by replay.
sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL hardening: remembered decisions stay bound to the original action boundary.

sourceLaws.title: Atomic Lookup Decision Commit
sourceLaws.failureMode: Lookup, prompt outcome, ledger write, and enforcement activation split apart under concurrency and create prompt loops or stale enforcement.
sourceLaws.detectionLogic: Treat lookup, user decision, ledger write, and enforcement activation as one witnessed atomic transition that either commits together or rolls back to the last known-good continuity state.
sourceLaws.stateForm: AtomicUPLTransition(path) => lookup + decision + witness_write + enforcement_activate OR rollback(snapshot).

sourceLaws.sourceBlock: Authored Agent Buccet time law from UPL hardening: lookup, decision, write, and activation commit atomically.

sourceLaws.title: Verified Domain Classification
